annotations.text:
What this is, and the one fact that changes every number on it.

The tip jar's price sheet — openTipSheet() in path/src/ui/tipJar.js, filled from the four live rows of path/src/tips.csv. Left column is what ships today; the two on the right are directions, each at desktop and at 390x844, because most of this game is played on a phone.

THE FONT. This sheet mounts on the BODY so it can sit over the splash, the pause menu and the score card. That puts it outside .sv-ui, so ui/typography.js never re-states its sizes: every px in tipJar.js is literal, unscaled by CONFIG.textStyles. But --sv-font IS written to the document element, so the sheet renders in the live tuned family — 'Press Start 2P'. A full em per glyph, and one weight only, so the font-weight: 700 on the title and the 600 on the labels do nothing at all. Size and colour carry the whole hierarchy.

Everything below was measured in a browser at these exact sizes, not estimated.

AS IT SHIPS — measured, not guessed.

Desktop: panel 614x616. Not 560 — there is no box-sizing rule in scope outside .sv-ui, so width: 560px is content and the 26px padding sits outside it. Rows 81px each, every one of the four descriptions wrapping to two lines in 337px. The footer is 108px, the tallest single block on the panel.

Phone (390x844): the panel is 359 wide and 814 tall outside its border, holding 824px of content in 812 — it SCROLLS, and what falls below the fold is the instruction. tipJar.js's own header calls that instruction the whole mechanism.

Rows come out 114.2 / 115.9 / 97.7 / 115.9, and that order is not a typo. Height here is not only the description: "Name seven seals" and "Your actual name" both WRAP at this width, so rows 2 and 4 carry a two-line label over a three-line description, while row 3 is the only one with a one-line label. The raggedness has two causes, not one.

AND A BUG WORTH FIXING WHATEVER ELSE HAPPENS: at 390px the title wraps to two lines and the 44px close button is absolutely positioned over it with nothing reserving room — the cross lands on top of the word "the". Both directions reserve a right gutter on the head.

A · RAIL — make it a price list, and keep the instruction on screen.

The description moves under the price instead of beside it and spans the row: 337px becomes 528px, and all four land on one line. The price becomes a right-aligned 4ch rail so $1 / $5 / $5 / $100 stack on their last digit — 4ch is exact, not generous, because this face is one em per glyph. The "Ko-fi ›" chevron goes: it was 85px of every row, four times, naming a place the footer already names. The four cards become hairline rules, so the warm hover is the only fill on the list.

AND THE FOOTER IS PINNED — the list scrolls, the instruction does not.

NOT ONE WORD IS REWRITTEN on this one. Every label, description and price is the live tips.csv string; the title, blurb and footer are tipJar.js's own, including "Tip the amount on Ko-fi and write the name in the message". That is what makes it the honest control for B.

Desktop 574x516, against the 614x616 it ships at: roomier per row and 100px shorter. Phone 696 of the 778 available — nothing scrolls, 82px in hand.

THE TRADEOFF: it is the conservative one. Nothing about what the panel says changes, so the footer is still the longest block on it — 126px on desktop, 181 on the phone. And $100 still reads like $1 in a uniform list; the joke lands flat.

B · TAGGED — put the instruction next to the thing it is about.

tips.csv already sorts every tier under SEAL or BOSS. Today that column is flattened away and the tag words are named once, in a paragraph four rows below the row they belong to. Here the tag is the heading it always was, and each group SHOWS the message the player is about to write rather than describing it.

SO THE FOOTER IS GONE ENTIRELY. Once a heading says "Your Ko-fi message: SEAL [the name]", a strip at the bottom was naming Ko-fi a third time and nothing else. The instruction was not deleted, it moved to where it is used.

The label leads and the price trails: inside a group you are choosing what to buy, not how much to spend. And the $100 tier is a CODA — out of the SEAL group, below BOSS, last — which is also exactly the order tips.csv gives (realname is row 4); grouping was the thing that had pulled it up. Out there it carries its own SEAL chip, because its tag really is SEAL and a row that cannot say which word to type arrives as a tip nobody can attribute.

Desktop 574x534. Phone 735 of 778, 43px spare, nothing scrolling.

THE COPY HERE IS ETHAN'S — the title, blurb and all four descriptions were rewritten in the canvas and are carried to both widths verbatim. They are shorter than the CSV strings, and that plus the deleted footer is why this fits a phone comfortably now; before those two changes it fit by a single pixel. Compare against A, which still quotes tips.csv exactly.

STILL TO SETTLE: the blurb reads unfinished — "...written by real mammals...contribute to the global mutual fund..." — and the BOSS group holds one row, which is honest and looks thin. It is also the bigger code change: openTipSheet() maps a flat array today.

Copy, and how this gets back into the game.

THE TWO DIRECTIONS NOW DIFFER IN COPY, deliberately. A quotes tips.csv and tipJar.js word for word — nothing on it is rewritten, so it is the control. B carries Ethan's rewrite: a new title ("Add a name to the pool."), a new blurb, and four new descriptions, at both widths.

Those are real content changes, not mockup text. If B is the direction, they are edits to the desc column of tips.csv and to the two strings in openTipSheet() — the panel title and the blurb.

The bracketed [the name], [prefix] [root] and [your real name] are placeholders for the player's own words, not names anybody has.

PORTING: this one does NOT go through design/styles.css. The tip jar carries its own injected stylesheet — the STYLES literal in path/src/ui/tipJar.js — and design/readme.md lists it under "Not in this bundle at all". Rules port to that literal; the markup changes (the grid rows, A's pinned footer, B's groups and coda) are edits to openTipSheet()'s template string in the same file. B additionally needs that flat tiers.map() grouped by tag. npm run test:tipjar covers it.
